findings.description:
FIND: `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.export_bundle()`, the block selecting `merkle_root` uses `epochs[-1]["merkle_root"]` whenever any epoch exists. `VerificationChain.build_inclusion_proof()` always builds proofs against the current full-record tree, not the last sealed epoch tree. In `verification_chain.py`, `build_inclusion_proof()` computes leaves from `self._records` with no epoch truncation, and embeds that full-tree root in the proof. Therefore if records were appended after the last sealed epoch, exported proofs are paired with a stale epoch root and will fail verification.
FOLLOW: This propagates through `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()`, which calls `self._chain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)`. For any chain with unsealed tail records after the last epoch, every exported bundle can be rendered unverifiable even though the chain itself is valid. The bug also falsifies the module docstring claim that bundles are “verifiable against a published epoch root” because the implementation is actually mixing full-chain proofs with epoch roots.
ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. The mismatch is directly observable from the two implementations.

        if epochs:
            merkle_root = epochs[-1]["merkle_root"]

            # No epoch sealed yet — compute from all records
            leaves = [_digest_bytes(r["chain_hash"]) for r in raw_records]
            merkle_root = "sha256:" + rfc9162_merkle_root(leaves).hex()
====

        # the current full-record tree.
        epochs = self._chain.epochs

findings.description:
FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()` lines 443-455, verification iterates with `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)`. `zip()` truncates to the shorter input silently. Evidence: Python `zip()` stops at the shortest iterable, so a bundle with 3 records and 2 proofs verifies only the first 2 pairs and never reports the missing proof for record 3. The method then returns success if those checked pairs pass. This is silently wrong output for the exported-audit feature.
FOLLOW: The bug affects the core bundle-verification path. Any consumer relying on `verify_bundle()` can accept malformed or incomplete bundles as valid. Because `EvidenceBundle.to_dict()` exposes separate `records` and `inclusion_proofs` arrays, accidental or malicious length mismatch is possible after serialization/deserialization. This also weakens confidence in `export_bundle()` regressions: truncated proofs can be masked instead of surfaced.

FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, `trace_finding()` claims a “chronological provenance trace” but returns events in sorted record-index order only (`for i in sorted(indices)`), not by `timestamp_utc`. Evidence from the implementation: no timestamp sort is performed before return. The chain context explicitly distinguishes append order from claimed wall-clock time; `VerificationChain` proves insertion order, not timestamp accuracy. Therefore “chronological” is incorrect as implemented whenever append order and timestamps differ, which can occur because `append_record()` accepts an explicit `timestamp` argument.
FOLLOW: This affects the provenance feature directly and also any reviewer using returned traces as temporal evidence. `_describe_event()` includes round/model semantics that imply timeline interpretation, so presenting append order as chronology is misleading. Bundle export by finding is also impacted indirectly when users expect trace order to match chronology before selecting records.

findings.description:
FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, `_classify_event()` lines 483-494 checks for verdict tokens only inside `model_chat_log` records. For `artifact_type == "verdict"`, it unconditionally returns `"verdict"` and never maps the record to `"confirmed"`, `"challenged"`, `"extended"`, or `"merged"`. Evidence: the code path for `atype == "verdict"` is a fixed return with no payload inspection, despite the module contract and focus area explicitly calling out identification of CONFIRM/CHALLENGE/EXTEND/MERGE. A verdict artifact containing `{"text": "CONFIRM C0042"}` will be traced generically, not semantically.
FOLLOW: Provenance traces lose the actual action semantics for explicit verdict records, so downstream audit output is incomplete and misleading. `_describe_event()` then falls through to the generic “referenced in verdict record” style for those records, which hides support/opposition relationships in the main review artifact. Query-by-finding still returns the record, but the feature “full lifecycle” does not fire cleanly.

FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, `_describe_event()` has no branch for `event_type == "verdict"`. Evidence: handled types are `submitted`, `confirmed`, `challenged`, `extended`, `merged`, `reported`, `checkpoint`, `health_scan`, and `policy`; then it falls back to `return f"Finding {finding_id} referenced in {rec.artifact_type} record"`. For records classified as `"verdict"`, the description becomes the generic fallback, losing artifact-specific semantics.
FOLLOW: This compounds F003. Even when a record is intentionally classified as `"verdict"`, the provenance output shown to the reviewer is vague and inconsistent with other event types. The trace feature degrades from “human-readable lifecycle” to generic references for a first-class artifact type.
findings.proposed_fix:
FIX

    if event_type == "policy":
        return f"Policy snapshot at round {rec.round_idx}"

    return f"Finding {finding_id} referenced in {rec.artifact_type} record"
====
    if event_type == "policy":
        return f"Policy snapshot at round {rec.round_idx}"
    if event_type == "verdict":
        return f"Verdict record for {finding_id} by {rec.model} in round {rec.round_idx}"

    return f"Finding {finding_id} referenced in {rec.artifact_type} record"

findings.description:
FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.query()` accepts an `experiment` filter, and `_EvidenceIndex` builds `by_experiment` from `record.metadata["experiment"]`, but `from_chain_file()` populates store-level experiment name from the directory name and `EvidenceRecord.from_chain_record()` leaves `experiment=""` when metadata omits it. Evidence: constructor stores `self._experiment = experiment_name`, yet records are not backfilled from that value. Result: `summary().experiment` can report a valid experiment name while `query(experiment=self._experiment)` returns no records for chains whose records lack per-record experiment metadata.
FOLLOW: This creates inconsistent entity partitioning across the main API surface. Store-level experiment identity, query-by-experiment, and export-by-filter no longer agree. Any consumer expecting “load store for experiment X, then query experiment X” can get empty results despite records being present, which breaks the advertised entity-indexed query feature.

====

        er.experiment = meta.get("experiment", "") or record.get("experiment", "")

findings.description:
FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, lines 325-327, `export_bundle` uses `self._chain.records` (deep copy) to compute leaves for Merkle root when no epochs exist, but uses `self._chain.records` again at line 336 to build inclusion proofs. The two calls produce different leaf lists if the chain was modified between them, breaking proof verification.

FOLLOW: When `self._chain.records` is called twice, it returns two different deep copies. If the underlying chain changes (e.g., another process appends records), the leaves list for root computation differs from leaves used for proof generation, making proofs unverifiable. This affects any bundle export on a live chain.

ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. The `VerificationChain.records` property returns `copy.deepcopy(self._records)`. Each call creates a new copy. Bundle verification will fail for chains without epochs if records change between the two calls.
findings.proposed_fix:
Compute leaves once and reuse:
<<<<
        # Get the Merkle root from the latest epoch, or compute it
        epochs = self._chain.epochs
        if epochs:
            merkle_root = epochs[-1]["merkle_root"]
        else:
            # No epoch sealed yet — compute from all records
            raw_records = self._chain.records  # Single call
            leaves = [_digest_bytes(r["chain_hash"]) for r in raw_records]
            merkle_root = "sha256:" + rfc9162_merkle_root(leaves).hex()

findings.description:
FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, lines 325-337, `export_bundle` computes Merkle root from `raw_records` (deep copy) when no epochs exist, but inclusion proofs are built from the live chain via `self._chain.build_inclusion_proof(i)`. The proof's embedded `merkle_root` field (from `build_inclusion_proof`) will be computed from current chain state, which may differ from the root computed from `raw_records`.

FOLLOW: `VerificationChain.build_inclusion_proof()` computes and embeds a `merkle_root` based on current chain leaves. If this differs from the root computed from `raw_records` (due to deep copy vs live data mismatch), bundle verification fails because `verify_inclusion_proof` compares embedded roots.

ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. Line 336 calls `self._chain.build_inclusion_proof(i)` which internally calls `rfc9162_merkle_root(leaves)` where `leaves = [_digest_bytes(r["chain_hash"]) for r in self._records]` (live records, not deep copy). The proof's `merkle_root` will be based on live records, while bundle's `merkle_root` is computed from `raw_records` (deep copy). Mismatch causes verification failure.
findings.proposed_fix:
Use consistent leaf source. Either:
1. Use `self._chain._records` directly (bypassing deep copy) for both root and proof computation, or
2. Compute root from the same leaves used in proof generation.

Simplest fix: Use live chain for both:
<<<<
        # Get the Merkle root from the latest epoch, or compute it
        epochs = self._chain.epochs
        if epochs:
            merkle_root = epochs[-1]["merkle_root"]
        else:
            # No epoch sealed yet — compute from current chain state
            leaves = [_digest_bytes(r["chain_hash"]) for r in self._chain._records]
            merkle_root = "sha256:" + rfc9162_merkle_root(leaves).hex()

findings.description:
FIND: In `bench/evidence.py`, lines 386-389, `_classify_event` uses `json.dumps(rec.payload)` to search for verdict strings like `"CONFIRM C0042"`. This fails when `rec.payload` contains JSON-serialized strings with escaped quotes, e.g., `{"text": "I CONFIRM C0042"}` becomes `"{\"text\": \"I CONFIRM C0042\"}"` in the JSON dump, breaking substring search.

FOLLOW: All provenance traces for findings with verdicts in nested text fields will misclassify events as "submitted" instead of "confirmed"/"challenged"/etc. This corrupts audit trails and misrepresents model behavior.

ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. JSON serialization escapes quotes, turning `"CONFIRM C0042"` into `\"CONFIRM C0042\"`. The substring search fails. This affects all `model_chat_log` records with structured payloads.

Additionally, `to_dict()` injects fields (`bundle_version`, `record_count`) not present in the dataclass definition, making instantiation via `EvidenceBundle(json_dict)` raise a `TypeError`. This prevents external auditors from easily loading an exported JSON bundle into an `EvidenceBundle` object to pass to `verify_bundle()`.
FOLLOW: The `verify_bundle` API is unusable for its primary purpose (external audit of exported JSON files), as users have no standard way to deserialize the file back into the required object type without manually stripping undocumented fields.
